name: transparent overlay autotile for the edges of a cracked concrete slab pavement on dirt: only the broken edge is drawn — rounded dirt bites eaten into the concrete from the open sides, a dark 1px broken lip under south breaks, lit broken rims, and loose concrete chunks lying on the dirt; the slab field underneath shows through so its seams and cracks run right up to the break
label: wasteland_ruins/slab-break

surfaces.part: dirt ground layer filling the whole sheet
concrete slab fragments seen from above (large slab at right, T/L-shaped strips at left and centre)
loose concrete chunks lying on the dirt

answer.evidence: The sheet is a flat, straight-down ground overlay. A dirt texture fills every row (width 256 on rows 0-191), with grey concrete fragments, seams and cracks drawn on it. The only dark edges are 1px broken lips and seam lines. There is no vertical front face of 3 or more rows, no eave or roof, and no ellipse. Column scans show only dirt, concrete and thin dark lip runs of 1-4 rows. The object reads as a flat floor decal with no front face.

styleAnswer.evidence: The concrete carries about 4 steps (light speckled body, mid grey, dark seam and lip, pale rim), against roughly 6 on the paving reference. The seam and lip lines lean cool grey-blue and the dirt bites have a brown edge, so the outline is tinted rather than black. The measured 0% near-neutral dark edge pixels supports this. Texture is real: speckled dither on the concrete, clod blotches on the dirt, and chunks lying loose, with 0% near-flat coverage and no 5x5 flat fills. Visible tones per tile are 5, which is above the grass reference (3) and a little below the paving reference (7). The palette is small, with only 12 colours in total, and the lower slab halves are fairly plain mid grey. That makes it slightly shallower than Beodeul, but it is still structurally sound and not a sticker look.

surfaces.part: concrete slab fragments (flat overlay of cracked pavement with dirt bites, seams and cracks)
loose concrete chunks and dirt ground fill

answer.evidence: The tile is a flat ground decal seen from above: concrete patches on a dirt field with seams and cracks drawn as thin lines. The only dark 1px lines are broken lips or seams, not a vertical face. No standing volume, front face of 3+ rows, or side face is drawn. The column scan shows only alternating dirt tones and thin dark lines. For a flat kind this is the expected top-down plate reading.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate has only 12 distinct colours in total and 5 visible tones per tile, against 7 on the paving reference. The concrete ramp is shallow: light grey, mid grey, a faint speckle tone and a dark seam or lip, with no clear per-chunk highlight, mid and deep stepping like the reference's stones and slabs. The dirt is only 2-3 browns of clumpy speckle, comparable to the grass reference. Dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the broken lip and seams lean grey-blue instead of using a sticker-black line. That is the one clear point in its favour. Near-flat coverage is 0%, so no large flat fills, and the speckle gives some texture. The chunks and breaks look ragged and blobby rather than the rounded bites described. The lit rims are weak, and the slab faces read as a uniform speckled grey. Overall it sits slightly below the reference's richness, so I fail it on the 'when in doubt' rule.

surfaces.part: cracked concrete slab fragments on dirt, seen from above as a flat overlay

answer.evidence: The image is a flat, top-down autotile overlay: broken concrete patches with seams and cracks on a dirt ground. It has no standing volume and no front (south) face of 3 or more rows. The dark 1px lips and the lit rims are edge details, not vertical faces. It matches the flat kind, so it reads as a top-down slab, which is correct for a ground decal.

styleAnswer.evidence: The candidate is a dirt field with concrete patches. It uses only 12 colours in total and 5 visible tones per tile, against 7 in the paving reference. Each material has a shallow ramp: the concrete reads as about 3-4 greys (light, mid, dark seam, speckle) and the dirt as about 3 browns plus a dark pit tone. The Beodeul paving and grass references carry about 6 steps per material. The edges are tinted, with 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outline is a dark material tone and not a black sticker line. There are no flat fills (0% near-flat). Speckle and grain are present, but the dirt is a fairly uniform repeated pit pattern. The concrete chunks have a few lit rims and dark lips but no per-stone shading, and they look thinner than the paving reference. Because the ramps are short and the density is below the paving reference, I fail it on the 'when in doubt' rule.

surfaces.part: dirt ground with concrete slab fragments and broken edges (flat overlay, seen from above)

answer.evidence: The whole tile is a flat ground decal seen from above. The silhouette is 256 px wide on every row, so it fills the tile. The column scan shows repeating dirt bands (L≈81 and L≈105) with 1px dark lines (L≈60) and concrete patches (L≈116 and L≈163). No band ends in a front-edge line with eave shadow, no ellipse is drawn, and nothing stands up. The dark 1px lips under south breaks and the chunks lying on the dirt are only thin outlines or flat bits, never a vertical face of 3 or more rows. This is a flat plate with no front face, which is correct for a flat floor decal.

styleAnswer.evidence: The concrete reads as about 4 steps: a lit rim, a light speckled body, a mid grey, and a dark lip and seam line. The paving reference has about 6-7 steps with per-stone shading. The measured facts show 5 visible tones per tile against 7 for paving, though that is above grass at 3. The candidate has only 12 distinct colours in total, so the slabs rely on one speckled light grey with little modelling. The dark edge pixels are 0% neutral, so the lip and seams carry a tint and are not a sticker-like black line. There are no flat 5x5 areas, because the speckle and dirt grain break them up, and the chunks and bites are shaped well. The concrete still looks thinner and flatter than the reference paving, and the larger slab faces have little tonal variation beyond the noise. It falls just short of the Beodeul bar for shading depth, so it fails.
